title: Can all rational beings agree under one law?
source_text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα εὐχήν τινα εἰπὼν τήν· εἰ γὰρ δὴ οἷόν τε εἰς ἕνα συμφρονῆσαι νόμον τοὺς τὴν Ἀσίαν καὶ Εὐρώπην καὶ Λιβύην Ἕλληνάς τε καὶ βαρβάρους ἄχρι περάτων νενεμημένους, ἀδύνατον τοῦτο νομίσας εἶναι ἐπιφέρει ὅτι ὁ τοῦτο οἰόμενος οἶδεν οὐδέν. εἰ δὲ χρὴ καὶ τοῦτ᾿ εἰπεῖν, λελέξεται ὀλίγα εἰς τὸν τόπον, δεόμενον πολλῆς ἐξετάσεως καὶ κατασκευῆς, εἰς τὸ φανῆναι οὐ μόνον δυνατὸν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀληθὲς τὸ λεγόμενον περὶ τοῦ εἰς ἕνα συμφρονῆσαι νόμον πᾶν τὸ λογικόν. οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς Στοᾶς. ἐπικρατήσαντος ὡς οἷόν τε τοῦ ἰσχυροτέρου τῶν ἄλλων στοιχείου, τὴν ἐκπύρωσιν ἔσεσθαι πάντων εἰς πῦρ μεταβαλλόντων, ἡμεῖς δὲ τῆς λογικῆς φύσεώς φαμεν ὅλης κρατῆσαί ποτε τὸν λόγον καὶ μεταποιῆσαι πᾶσαν ψυχὴν εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ τελειότητα, ἐπὰν ἕκαστος ψιλῇ χρησάμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ἕληται ἃ βούλεται καὶ γένηται ἐν οἷς εἵλατο· καὶ φαμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν εἰκὸς, ὥσπερ ἐπὶ τῶν (ἐν) τοῖς σώμασι νοσημάτων καὶ τραυμάτων τινὰ τῶν συμβαινόντων ἰσχυρότερα εἶναι πάσης ἰατρικῆς τέχνης, οὕτως ἐπὶ τῶν ψυχῶν εἶναί τι τῶν ἀπὸ κακίας ἀδύνατον ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσι λογικοῦ καὶ θεοῦ θεραπευθῆναι. πάντων γὰρ τῶν ἐν ψυχῇ κακῶν δυνατώτερος ὢν ὁ λόγος καὶ ἡ ἐν αὐτῷ θεραπεία προσάγει κατὰ βούλησιν θεοῦ ἑκάστῳ αὐτὴν, καὶ τὸ τέλος τῶν πραγμάτων ἀναιρεθῆναί ἐστι τὴν κακίαν· πότερον δὲ ὥστε μηδαμῇ μηδαμῶς ἔτι αὐ τὴν ἐπιτραπῆναι δύνασθαι ἢ μὴ, οὐ τοῦ παρόντος ἐστὶ λόγου διδάξαι. πολλὰ μὲν ουν αἱ προφητεῖαι περὶ τῆς παντελοῦς ἀναιρέσεως τῶν κακῶν καὶ διορθώσεως πάσης ψυχῆς ἐν ἀποῤῥήτοις λέγουσιν, ἀρκεῖ δ᾿ ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος παραθέσθαι τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ Σοφονίου λέξιν, οὕτως ἔχουσαν· „ἑτοιμάζου, ὄρθρισον· διέφθαρται πᾶσα ἡ ἐπιφυλλὶς αὐτῶν. διὰ τοῦτο ὑπόμεινόν (με) , λέγει κύριος, ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστάσεώς μου εἰς μαρτύριον· διότι τὸ κρίμα μου εἰς συναγωγὰς ἐθνῶν τοῦ ἐκδέξασθαι βασιλεῖς, τοῦ ἐκχέαι ἐπ᾿ αὐτοὺς πᾶσαν ὀργὴν θυμοῦ μου. ἐν γὰρ πυρὶ ζήλου μου καταναλωθήσεται πᾶσα ἡ γῆ· ὅτι τότε μεταστρέψω ἐπὶ λαοὺς γλῶσσαν εἰς γενεὰν αὐτῆς, τοῦ ἐπικαλεῖσθαι πάντας τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου, τοῦ δουλεύειν (αὐτῷ) ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἕνα. ἐκ περάτων ποταμῶν Αἰθιοπίας θύσουσι θυσίας μοι. ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇς ἐκ πάντων τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων σου, ὧν ἠσέβησας εἰς ἐμέ· ὅτι τότε περιελῶ ἀπὸ σοῦ τὰ φαυλίσματα τῆς ὕβρεώς σου, καὶ οὐκ ἔτι μὴ προσθῇς τοῦ μεγαλαυχῆσαι ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος τὸ ἅγιόν μου. καὶ ὑπολείψομαι ἐν σοὶ λαὸν πραῢν καὶ ταπεινὸν, καὶ εὐλαβηθήσονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ὀνόματος κυρίου οἱ κατάλοιποι τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ οὐ ποιήσουσιν ἀδικίαν καὶ οὐ λαλήσουσι μάταια, καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν γλῶσσα δολία· διότι αὐτοὶ νεμήσονται καὶ κοιτασθήσονται, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἐκφοβῶν αὐτούς.“ ὁ δυνάμενος δ᾿ εἰς ταῦτα ὅλα μὲν κατανοήσας τὴν σαφήνειαν τῆς προφητείας παραστησάτω, μάλιστα δ᾿ ἐξετασάτω, τί τὸ ἀναλουμένης πάσης τῆς γῆς μεταστραφῆναι „ἐπὶ λαοὺς γλῶσσαν εἰς γενεὰν αὐτῆς,“ ἀνάλογον τοῖς πρὸ τῆς συγχύσεως πράγμασι· καὶ κατανοησάτω, τί τὸ „ἐπικαλεῖσθαι πάντας τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου, τοῦ δουλεύειν αὐτῷ ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἕνα,“ ὡς περιαιρεθῆναι „τὰ τῆς ὕβρεως φαυλίσματα,“ καὶ μηκέτι εἶναι „ἀδικίαν“ μηδὲ λόγους ματαίους μηδὲ γλῶσσαν δολίαν. ταῦτα δ᾿ ἔδοξέ μοι μετρίως καὶ οὐ μετὰ τῆς ἀκριβοῦς διηγήσεως παραθέσθαι διὰ τὴν Κέλσου λέξιν, οἰομένου τὸ συμφρονῆσαι τοὺς τὴν Ἀσίαν καὶ Εὐρώπην καὶ Λιβύην Ἕλληνάς τε καὶ βαρβάρους οἰκοῦντας ἀδύνατον εἶναι. καὶ τάχα ἀληθῶς ἀδύνατον μὲν τὸ τοιοῦτο τοῖς ἔτι ἐν σώμασι, οὐ μὴν ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀπολυθεῖσιν αὐτῶν.
pass_a_gloss: After these things, having spoken a certain prayer/wish (εὐχή): [Celsus] 'for if indeed it were possible for those dwelling-distributed (νέμω, pf. pass.) over Asia and Europe and Libya, Greeks and barbarians, to the limits (πέρας), to agree in mind (συμφρονέω) into one law (νόμος)'; thinking this to be impossible he adds that 'the one thinking this knows nothing'. [Origen] If this too must be said, a few things will be said on the topic (τόπος), which needs much examination (ἐξέτασις) and construction/proof (κατασκευή), so that what is said about all the rational (τὸ λογικόν) agreeing into one law appears not only possible but also true. Those from the Stoa [say]: the stronger of the other elements (στοιχεῖον) having prevailed (ἐπικρατέω) as far as possible, there will be the conflagration (ἐκπύρωσις), all things changing into fire. But we say the Word/Reason (λόγος) will at some time master (κρατέω) the whole rational nature (φύσις) and re-make (μεταποιέω) every soul into his own perfection (τελειότης), when each, using bare/mere (ψιλός) authority/freedom (ἐξουσία), chooses (αἱρέομαι) what he wills (βούλομαι) and comes to be in what he chose. And we say it is not likely (εἰκός) that, as with diseases (νόσημα) and wounds (τραῦμα) in bodies some of the happenings are stronger than every medical art (ἰατρικὴ τέχνη), so with souls something of those from wickedness (κακία) is impossible to be healed (θεραπεύω) by the [Word] over all and God. For being more powerful than all the evils in the soul, the Word and the healing (θεραπεία) in him brings it near (προσάγω) to each according to the will (βούλησις) of God, and the end (τέλος) of things is that wickedness be taken away/destroyed (ἀναιρέω). Whether so that it can no longer anywhere in any way (μηδαμῇ μηδαμῶς) be permitted (ἐπιτρέπω) or not, is not for the present discourse to teach. The prophecies say many things in secret/unspeakable terms (ἐν ἀπορρήτοις) about the complete destruction (ἀναίρεσις) of evils and correction (διόρθωσις) of every soul; it suffices for the present to set beside (παρατίθημι) the wording (λέξις) from Zephaniah: [Zeph 3:7-13 LXX: 'prepare, rise early (ὀρθρίζω); all their gleaning (ἐπιφυλλίς) is destroyed; therefore wait for me, says the Lord, in the day of my rising-up (ἀνάστασις) for a testimony (μαρτύριον); because my judgment (κρίμα) is for gatherings (συναγωγή) of nations, to receive (ἐκδέχομαι) kings, to pour out on them all the wrath of my anger (ὀργὴ θυμοῦ); for in fire of my jealousy (ζῆλος) all the earth will be consumed (καταναλίσκω); for then I will turn (μεταστρέφω) upon/for peoples a tongue (γλῶσσα) into its generation (γενεά), that all call upon (ἐπικαλέομαι) the name of the Lord, to serve (δουλεύω) him under one yoke (ζυγός); from the limits of rivers of Ethiopia they will sacrifice (θύω) sacrifices to me; in that day you will not be shamed (καταισχύνω) from all your practices (ἐπιτήδευμα) by which you acted impiously (ἀσεβέω) against me; for then I will remove (περιαιρέω) from you the paltry things (φαύλισμα) of your insolence (ὕβρις), and no more will you add to boast (μεγαλαυχέω) on my holy mountain; and I will leave in you a people meek (πραΰς) and lowly (ταπεινός), and the remnant of Israel will reverence (εὐλαβέομαι) from the name of the Lord, and will not do injustice (ἀδικία), nor speak vain things (μάταια), and a deceitful (δόλιος) tongue will not be found in their mouth; for they will pasture (νέμομαι) and lie down (κοιτάζομαι), and there will be none frightening them']. Let the one able, having understood (κατανοέω) all these, present the clarity (σαφήνεια) of the prophecy, and most of all examine what is the being turned, all the earth being consumed, 'upon peoples a tongue into its generation', analogous to the things before the confusion (σύγχυσις); and consider what is 'all calling upon the name of the Lord, to serve him under one yoke', so that 'the paltry things of insolence' be removed and there no longer be 'injustice', nor vain words, nor deceitful tongue. These things seemed good to me to set out moderately (μετρίως) and not with exact exposition (ἀκριβὴς διήγησις) because of Celsus's wording, who thinks it impossible for the Greeks and barbarians inhabiting Asia, Europe and Libya to agree. And perhaps truly such a thing is impossible for those still in bodies, but not impossible for those released (ἀπολύω) from them.
pass_b_english: After this he utters a kind of wish: “If only it were possible for the Greeks and barbarians who inhabit Asia, Europe and Libya, to their farthest bounds, to come to agreement under one law!” Then, judging this impossible, he adds that “whoever thinks this knows nothing.”

If something must be said on this too, a few things will be said on the subject, though it needs much examination and proof, to show that what is said about every rational being coming to agree under one law is not only possible but true. The Stoics say that when the element which is stronger than the others has prevailed, as far as it can, the conflagration will come, with all things changing into fire. But we say that the Word will one day gain mastery over the whole of rational nature and transform every soul into his own perfection, when each one, using nothing but his own freedom, chooses what he wills and comes to be in what he has chosen.

And we say that it is not reasonable to think that, as with diseases and wounds in the body some of the things that happen prove stronger than the whole art of medicine, so with souls some effect of wickedness cannot be healed by the Word, who is over all and is God. For the Word is mightier than all the evils in the soul, and so is the healing that is in him, and he applies it to each one according to the will of God; and the end of things is that wickedness be destroyed. Whether it will be destroyed so that it can never again, anywhere or in any way, be permitted, or not, it is not the task of the present discussion to teach.

Now the prophecies say many things, in veiled terms, about the complete destruction of evils and the setting right of every soul; for the present it is enough to set out the passage from Zephaniah, which runs thus: “Make ready, rise early: all their gleaning is ruined. Therefore wait for me, says the Lord, on the day of my rising up for a testimony; for my judgment is upon the gatherings of the nations, to receive kings, to pour out upon them all the wrath of my anger. For in the fire of my jealousy all the earth shall be consumed. For then I will turn for the peoples a tongue into its own generation, so that all may call upon the name of the Lord and serve him under one yoke. From the ends of the rivers of Ethiopia they shall offer sacrifices to me. On that day you shall not be put to shame for all your practices by which you acted impiously against me; for then I will take away from you the contemptible things of your insolence, and you shall no longer go on boasting upon my holy mountain. And I will leave in you a people meek and lowly, and the remnant of Israel shall reverence the name of the Lord; and they shall do no wrong and speak no vain things, and no deceitful tongue shall be found in their mouth; for they shall feed and lie down, and there shall be no one to make them afraid” (Zephaniah 3:7–13).

Let anyone who is able, having studied all of this, set out the clear meaning of the prophecy; and let him examine above all what it means that, when all the earth is being consumed, a tongue is turned “for the peoples into its own generation” (Zephaniah 3:9), in a way that answers to the state of things before the confusion (Genesis 11:7–9). And let him consider what it means for “all to call upon the name of the Lord and serve him under one yoke” (Zephaniah 3:9), so that “the contemptible things of insolence” are taken away (Zephaniah 3:11), and there is no longer “wrong,” nor vain words, nor a deceitful tongue (Zephaniah 3:13).

I have thought it right to set these things out briefly and without a precise exposition, because of Celsus’s statement, since he thinks it impossible for the Greeks and barbarians who live in Asia, Europe and Libya to come to agreement. And perhaps such a thing truly is impossible for those who are still in bodies, but not impossible for those who have been set free from them.

choices.choice: Celsus’s wish and his remark ‘whoever thinks this knows nothing’ are in double quotation marks. ‘Libya’ is the Greek name for Africa; kept as written. The Stoic sentence lacks a main verb in the transmitted text (οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς Στοᾶς ... τὴν ἐκπύρωσιν ἔσεσθαι); ‘say’ is supplied from the parallel φαμεν that follows, and the staged text’s full stop after Στοᾶς is treated as a comma. ἐπὰν ἕκαστος ... ἕληται ἃ βούλεται: the subject of βούλεται is ambiguous (the individual, or the Word); English ‘chooses what he wills’ keeps the same ambiguity. ψιλῇ ... τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ rendered ‘using nothing but his own freedom’ (choice without compulsion). Doubtful reading: the staged text has ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσι λογικοῦ καὶ θεοῦ; the sense requires λόγου (‘the Word who is over all and is God’), and the next sentence names ὁ λόγος as the healer, so this is translated as λόγου; check against the Koetschau page. ὁ λόγος καὶ ἡ ἐν αὐτῷ θεραπεία προσάγει ... αὐτήν is grammatically loose; rendered so that both the Word and his healing are ‘mightier’, and the Word applies the healing. ἐπιτραπῆναι (‘be permitted’) is translated as printed; some may suspect ἐπιστραφῆναι (‘return’), which is not adopted. ἐν ἀπορρήτοις rendered ‘in veiled terms’. Zephaniah: Origen quotes the Septuagint of Zephaniah 3:7b–13 (verse numbers agree with the English Bible here). His text differs slightly from the common LXX: ἐν ἡμέρᾳ (LXX εἰς ἡμέραν), τοῦ ἐκδέξασθαι (LXX εἰσδέξασθαι), θύσουσι θυσίας (LXX οἴσουσιν θυσίας), ζήλου (LXX ζήλους); the LXX differs widely from the Hebrew (e.g. ‘gleaning’, ‘my rising up for a testimony’, ‘a tongue into its own generation’ where the Hebrew has ‘a pure lip’). The obscure phrase μεταστρέψω ἐπὶ λαοὺς γλῶσσαν εἰς γενεὰν αὐτῆς is kept close (‘turn for the peoples a tongue into its own generation’) because Origen reads it as a return to the single speech before Babel. ‘Before the confusion’ (πρὸ τῆς συγχύσεως) alludes to the confusion of tongues at Babel, cited Genesis 11:7–9. In the summary, μηδὲ λόγους ματαίους μηδὲ γλῶσσαν δολίαν paraphrases Zephaniah 3:13 rather than quoting it, so only ‘wrong’ is in quotation marks. Reviewer: the source TEI (origen_celsum.xml, line 20108, at page mark r 214) also reads λογικοῦ, so the λόγου rendering is a departure from the copy-text that no local witness supports; no Koetschau GCS 2-3 scan is in the repo to check the printed page.
Celsus's wish: one participle νενεμημένους no longer doubled as 'live in' + 'spread out'; ἄχρι περάτων as 'to their farthest bounds' (no added 'earth')
εἰ δὲ χρὴ καὶ τοῦτ᾿ εἰπεῖν: 'If something must be said on this too' (εἰπεῖν = say, not 'answer')
οὐκ ἔστιν εἰκὸς ... εἶναί τι: smoothed 'there is any of the effects' to 'some effect of wickedness cannot be healed'
Zephaniah 3:7-13 checked verse by verse against LXX (start 3:7 ἑτοιμάζου ὄρθρισον, end 3:13 ὁ ἐκφοβῶν); 3:9, 3:11, 3:13 and Genesis 11:7-9 (σύγχυσις) confirmed
